A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OOMB study. All 40 pages of each, including Appendices A–B, support reliable comparison; relocated prompt tables and abbreviated examples can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of ten LLMs on opinion extraction and insight generation, alongside annotation-agreement analyses and human evaluations (Tables 2–6; Figure 6).

after.justification: v3 retains the original model evaluations, annotation-agreement results, human evaluations and supplementary analyses reported in v2.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, FOE/OIG procedures, zero-shot prompting and Contextual Match procedure are unchanged. The task and annotation prompts retain the same instructions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 600 automotive examples from blogs, Reddit, review sites and YouTube for the same two tasks (Tables 1 and 7). Shortened excerpts in Table 29 do not indicate changed dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The same ten GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Llama3, Gemma2, Qwen2.5 and DeepSeek variants participate in corresponding comparisons. Model subsets in the supplementary analyses also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Zero-shot evaluation, generation temperatures, matching thresholds, metrics and human/LLM-judge sampling designs remain unchanged (Sections 3–4 and Appendix B). Relocated judge prompts contain the same evaluation instructions.

E4.justification: The threshold sensitivity, multiple-inference, input-complexity and gold-tuple analyses are retained (Tables 8–9; Figures 3, 5–6). The same extraction and generation cases and their outcomes remain; changes concern excerpting and explanatory commentary.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain the same agreement/correlation analyses and p-value reporting. No seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures are added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends and case ratings match. For example, GPT-4o retains 48.28 CM F1 in Table 3, and the two OIG cases retain A3CU scores of 60.91 and 10.12 in Tables 30–31.

T1.justification: The formal task and tuple definitions and Relaxed Match decision rule in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version introduces or removes theoretical assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about LLM extraction and abstraction capabilities. Rewording the RQ2 heading does not change its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Tables 32–33 abbreviate case-specific judge explanations. Table 32 omits the criticism that the insight should better explain Google OS advantages and the SUV’s distinctive design. The main interpretations and Limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, hardware, data-source disclosures, annotation instructions and code/data access information are retained. Tables 16–28 preserve the same experimental and annotation prompts despite formatting and placement changes.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. OOMB retains the same positioning relative to extraction-focused benchmarks and the same novelty claims.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand the affiliation, revise RQ2 wording, standardize evaluation/task labels and abbreviate prose in Tables 29, 32 and 33. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 removes printed page numbers, makes small alignment edits to Figure 2, and reformats and redistributes appendix prompt tables. Tables 29, 32 and 33 use shorter excerpts with ellipses. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and principal conclusions are unchanged. Wording and layout refinements provide limited presentation benefits, while abbreviated appendix examples and rationales remove some explanatory detail. These localized changes do not meaningfully alter the paper’s overall reliability or usefulness.
